newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia to export 17m tonnes of wheat - AWB.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia to export 17m tonnes of wheat - AWB.

text.p: Australia was looking to export about 17.0 million tonnes of wheat from its current bumper crop, up from shipments of 13.3 million tonnes from the previous crop, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) told Reuters.
The 17.0 million tonne export forecast was based on the latest crop estimate of 21.0 million tonnes, Alex Nichol, AWB communications manager, said.

The AWB export forecast updates a mid-October forecast by the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) of total Australian wheat exports of 13.43 million tonnes for the marketing year ending September 30, 1997.
ABARE's export forecast assumed a 3.46 million tonnes increase in stocks for 1996/97, against a 110,000 tonnes increase in 1995/96.

GrainCorp, the New South Wales (NSW) state grain handling cooperative, issued a statement on Friday which said exports of between four and five million tonnes of grain were expected from the state from the current crop.
"This will be one of the largest grain export programmes from NSW in a single year," managing director Tom Keene said.
Last year the state exported close to two million tonnes of grain.
GrainCorp had received more than 800,000 tonnes of grain into its system since the start of the present harvest, the statement said.
"All we need now is good hot, dry weather to cap off what has been a great season," Keene said.
"Many growers reported that they have produced their best crops ever and if they come off in good condition it will be a real boost to them and rural NSW," he said.
It was estimated that the state would produce more than eight million tonnes of grain from current crops, with GrainCorp's storage system likely to receive about 6.5 million tonnes, he said.
To receive the harvest, GrainCorp would open 202 sites, operate more than 100 bunkers and employ 1,500 casual staff in addition to its permanent workforce of 450, he said.
The group has injected more than A$18.0 million into silo improvements and extended operational hours at silos.
